name: @cloudsforge/backup-runner
description: The DATA PLANE of estate backup and restore. Leases backup.* jobs out of admin_api's queue, dumps twenty-nine databases and the volumes worth keeping, and never — by construction — touches the custody keyring. admin-api owns the catalogue and the authority; this owns the bytes.
_localDependencies: Every sibling takes 'link:', not 'file:', for the reason admin-api/package.json spells out: a
'file:' path PACKS the dependency, and each of these packages declares files: ['dist'] with a
publishConfig pointing main/types at a dist/ that has not been built.
The paths are '../../runtime' rather than admin-api's '../runtime' because this deployable lives
one directory deeper — deploy/backup, not a repository root beside runtime/.
_whyTwoDsns: BACKUP_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL and BACKUP_CLUSTER_URL are two connection strings in one process, and
that is the entire reason this is a separate deployable rather than four more handlers inside
admin-api. Rule 1 gives a service one database and CI greps admin-api/src for a second DSN.
A process that must read all twenty-nine databases in the cluster cannot satisfy that rule and
should not: reading every database is a different trust domain from composing an operator's
console, and keeping them in one process would give an admin-api RCE the whole estate.
